catalog_quote: 2.3 Ton. Le système tonal comprend deux niveaux: bas (à, àa) et haut (á, áa); en plus il faut distinguer le ton tombant (â, âà) qui n'apparaît que sous certaines conditions établies par D. Abdoullaye et J. Kelly (1985). Voici quelques exemples de paires minimales: bâggò 'sauterelle' : bàggò 'terrasser'; bóoló 'vider' : bòolò 's'incliner'; 'óosó 'mettre le feu' : 'òòsò 'porter sur l'épaule'; dìyyè 'oreille' : dìyyé 'a cherché'; páató 'soleil' : pàatò 'écarter les jambes'; táppó 'rassembler' : tàppò 'traverser'; gêllú 'penis' : gèllú 'que tu ris'; 'óomó 'mordre' : 'òomò 'sortir'. ... 2.4 Syllabe. La syllabe migama est soit ouverte (CV, CVV), soit fermée (CVC, CVVC). [p. 17: Le système phonologique du migama comprend 24 phonèmes consonantiques et 5 phonèmes vocaliques.]

new_statements.translation: 2.3 Tone. The tonal system comprises two levels: low (à, àa) and high (á, áa); in addition one must distinguish the falling tone (â, âà), which appears only under certain conditions established by D. Abdoullaye and J. Kelly (1985). Here are some examples of minimal pairs: bâggò 'grasshopper' : bàggò 'to knock down'; bóoló 'to empty' : bòolò 'to bow'; 'óosó 'to set fire' : 'òòsò 'to carry on the shoulder'; dìyyè 'ear' : dìyyé 'searched'; páató 'sun' : pàatò 'to spread the legs' [...]. [p. 17: The phonological system of Migama comprises 24 consonant phonemes and 5 vowel phonemes.]

new_statements.rule_in_words: Migaama is described as a two-level tone language (low vs. high on short and long vowels) with a conditioned falling tone; tone is lexically and grammatically contrastive (minimal pairs on nouns and verbs). The description contains no statement about word stress or accent at all — the phonology notes go straight from vowels to tone to syllable structure, and no stress marking is used in the lexicon (tone marks only). So: tonal, source silent on stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None regarding stress. For tone: the falling tone occurs only under conditions set out in Abdoullaye & Kelly 1985 (not opened).
new_statements.domain_note: Word-level lexical tone on citation forms (nouns and verb stems, with plural/aspect forms in parentheses); verb-stem tonal patterns treated separately in §3.3.3.3. Dialect described is the Migama of Baro (p. 16: 'Le dialecte choisi ici est le migama de Baro').
new_statements.identity_note: Source describes 'le migama de Baro' (Baro, canton chief-town; p. 16 explicitly chooses this dialect as the most widely spoken), i.e. the Nuclear Migaama dialect in Glottolog's list (Dambiya, Doga, Gamiya, Nuclear Migaama; no separate dialect glottocode confirmed). The source notes the three parlers (Baro, doga, gamiya) differ 'surtout au niveau tonal et morphologique'. Migaama = Djonkor Abou Telfane; distinct from Jonkor Bourmataguil [jeu] and from Mukulu/'Djonkor Guéra'.

sources.note: Section 2 'Notes phonologiques' (pp. 17-21) covers consonants, vowels (short/long), tone (2.3: two level tones low and high plus a conditioned falling tone, referring to Abdoullaye & Kelly 1985 for the conditions; minimal pairs given) and syllable structure. No section, sentence or word on accent/stress; scanned of the whole grammatical introduction (pp. 15-55) has zero hits for 'accent'. Verb chapter has only a tonal-structure section (3.3.3.3). Lexical entries are marked for tone only.
